assistant.name: Galton
starters: What happens to what we keep if we hire a seventh technician at $5,800 a month?
What if we raise the service call to $210?
Can we get through a slow spring if sales run 15% under last year?
What if Quinn R. moves from a 40% split to a $5,400 salary?
What does buying a $38,000 van in week 4 do to cash and to our tax?
What if I take $6,000 a month of my draw as salary instead?
sectorNotes: A new technician usually takes two to three months to reach a full schedule. For the first months, about half of a typical technician's sales is a fair figure; say which one you used.
AC repair peaks from June to August and furnace repair from November to February.
Parts and materials are a cost of each job. They do not go up when the price goes up.
A subcontractor on a split is paid a percent of the jobs they bill; an employee on salary is paid the same whatever the month's sales.
Meals bought for crews and customers are only partly deductible, so a busy season with a lot of crew meals adds a little to taxable income.
Fines and penalties, such as parking tickets on service calls, are not deductible.
Vans, trucks and diagnostic tools are bought in lumps. How fast their cost is written off for tax is a choice to make with the accountant before the year ends, not after.
